input.brief: Simplify IT: one-person data analytics studio in Katowice — dashboards, reporting automation, SQL/Python, turning messy spreadsheets into one clear number

direction.name: The printed annual
direction.idea: Lay the page out like a well-designed printed report or magazine feature: a masthead image, a tight oversized title, text held to a strict column line, and colour used in solid blocks the way a two-colour print job would. It gives weight and authority to subjects that are really about content: findings, a manifesto, a programme, a serious product. The reader should feel that someone edited this.
direction.composition: A fixed vertical axis at about 42% of the viewport width organises everything: headings begin on it, body columns hang from it, and the 0–42% zone holds small side notes, figures or stays empty. Masthead: a wide image band (photographic mosaic or a single crop) across the top 45% of the first screen; below it the title at 7–9vw starting on the axis, with a two-sentence standfirst at 20–24px. Sections alternate between text pages (title on the axis, body in one or two columns of 34–40ch to its right) and full-bleed colour pages carrying one large figure, quotation or image mosaic. Mosaics are gutterless: photographs and flat colour tiles butted together in a 4- or 6-cell grid. Page numbers, running heads and other print furniture are left out.
direction.typography: A tight heavy grotesk or a sharp serif for titles; an excellent text face for reading at 18–20px with leading near 1.5. Headings in sentence case, tracked tight.
direction.colour: Paper, ink and two or three solid block colours. A colour page is a whole section in one flat colour.
direction.imagery: Photographs used as blocks in mosaics alongside flat colour tiles; mixed subjects are fine if cropped tight and converted to one treatment.
direction.photoTreatment: Give all photographs in a mosaic one treatment: greyscale via `filter: grayscale(1) contrast(1.05)`, or all full colour. Do not mix.
direction.richness: The column line, the mosaics and whole pages of colour give structure and variety without ornaments.
direction.pitfalls: The axis must be exact and reused everywhere or it reads as random indentation. Keep paragraphs to a real reading measure. On a phone the axis collapses to the left margin and side notes move inline above their paragraph.

hero.name: Narrow talk, wide headline
hero.blueprint: An asymmetric sheet on one flat paper-grey ground, divided at 34% of the width by alignment only. Left column (columns 1-4, 32px margin): the wordmark top-left; then, starting at 30% of the height, one supporting sentence at 22px with leading 1.35, max 24ch; under it the single action, a solid ink rectangle with square corners. The column's lower third is empty. Right column (columns 5-12): four text links at 15px on its top edge, the first aligned exactly to the 34% line. Beneath them the headline in a very heavy grotesk at clamp(88px, 9.8vw, 150px), two lines, line-height 0.82, tracking -0.04em, flush left on the 34% line and filling the column width. A square-cornered photograph the full width of the right column starts at 68% of the viewport height and is cropped by the bottom edge. A solid accent block 260px wide, carrying one real figure at 40px and one line of text, overlaps the photograph's top-left corner by half its own height using a negative top margin.
hero.mobile: One column on 20px margins. The wordmark and a menu word share the top row. The headline comes first at 15vw on two lines, heavy, line-height 0.85. The supporting sentence follows at 18px, then the action at full width. The photograph runs full bleed below at 4:3, with the accent block overlapping its top-left corner at 60% of the screen width.
hero.headline: A 2-4 word statement in the heaviest weight, at most 20 characters, one or two words per line.

type.note: One neo-grotesk doing everything: semibold headings pulled tight, small regular text, no capitals and no second voice. Suits software, hardware and studio pages that want to look exact and unshowy.

palette.name: Orange and black
palette.note: Hot orange is the page: one flat field with blue-black type, flipping at a hard horizontal seam to a white section when the content needs a rest. The button is a solid block of the same blue-black with orange text, and every other colour comes from the objects shown.

photos.title: People
photos.note: figures, silhouettes and portraits, mostly unposed
photos.treatment: Give all photographs in a mosaic one treatment: greyscale via `filter: grayscale(1) contrast(1.05)`, or all full colour. Do not mix.

motion.name: Masked headline
motion.description: On load, each line of the headline rises from behind its own baseline, about 900ms with a strong ease-out, the second line 110ms after the first; the supporting sentence and the action then fade up together. Nothing else on the page performs. Because headlines are two lines at most, you author the line breaks and wrap each line yourself. Recipe: 'Masked line reveal' in references/motion.md.

sections.name: Title, note, facts row
sections.blueprint: First row: a heading of two to four words in a light weight at clamp(44px, 5vw, 76px) sits on the left margin in columns 1–6; a three-line paragraph at 16px, 260px wide, sits in columns 10–12 with its last line on the heading's baseline. Columns 7–9 stay empty. 120px lower, a second row sets three or four facts (a date, a time, a place, a price) as large light text at clamp(28px, 3vw, 44px), spread across the 12 columns with `justify-content: space-between`. Each fact has a one-line explanation at 14px directly under it in the soft ink, left-aligned to the fact. Facts are separated only by the space between them, so the row reads like the line of times on a printed programme. A photograph may start under the right half of the facts row, 5 columns wide at 4:3. Padding 140px top, 120px bottom.
sections.mobile: Heading at 11vw on the left margin; the note follows directly under it at 16px, full width. The facts become a two-column grid with a 32px row gap, each fact at 26px with its explanation beneath. Any photograph goes last, full width.

sections.name: Band of unequal panels
sections.blueprint: A modest heading, then one wide band of pictures. The heading, two to four words at 36–44px, starts at column 3, left of centre, with 64px beneath it. The band spans the full viewport width edge to edge and is 68svh tall: four photographs standing side by side with no gaps and deliberately unequal widths, a flex row with flex-grow values of 5, 2, 3 and 2. Each panel is cropped with object-fit: cover to a tall slice, so the band reads as one folded view. The first panel carries a two-line title at 28px in paper colour at its top-left, 24px in, over a neutral scrim that covers only that corner. Hovering a panel raises its flex-grow to 6 over 500ms while the others give way; without hover the widths simply stay. One caption line at 16px sits under the band at the left margin.
sections.mobile: The heading sits on the margin at 28px. The band becomes a two-by-two block with no gaps, 84svh tall in total: the first row split 64/36 and the second 36/64, so the slices stay unequal. The title stays on the first panel. No hover behaviour.

sections.name: Stages as one bar
sections.blueprint: The product's progress bar, enlarged until it spans the page, is the diagram. One bar runs across columns 1–12, 22vh tall, built as a flex row of three or four solid segments with 6px gaps, root marked data-ui. Each segment's width follows how long that stage really takes (flex-grow from the true durations, 12% minimum), and each is a different flat palette colour, so the reader sees at once that signing up is a sliver and the rest is the product working. Inside every segment, top-left with 20px padding, its duration in words at clamp(20px, 2vw, 30px): 'Two minutes', 'About a day'. Under each segment, on its left edge, one clause at 17px, 22ch wide, beginning with its order word. Above the bar, 64px clear of it, the heading: two to five words at clamp(48px, 6.4vw, 104px), flush left. Nothing else.
sections.mobile: The bar turns vertical: segments stack as full-width blocks whose heights keep the proportions, 72px minimum, 6px gaps, about 70svh in total. Each holds its duration at 22px top-left and its clause at 16px beneath. The heading sits above at 11vw on two lines.

sections.name: Cards that fold into spines
sections.blueprint: For a journal, a run of notes or a list of chapters without pictures. A wrapper about 400svh tall holds a sticky stage of 100svh. The heading, two to four words at clamp(48px, 4.2vw, 64px), sits top-left on the 32px margin, 120px from the top. Under it a band 360px tall spans the content width and holds a horizontal deck of text cards, each about 620px wide, in three neighbouring flat tones of one hue taken in turn. On a card, with 32px padding: its title at 30px on up to two lines, leading 1.1; an excerpt of two lines at 16px; and along the bottom edge the date on the left and a text link to read it on the right, both at 16px. As the page scrolls, each step slides the next card in from the right edge and squeezes the earlier ones into slivers 120px wide stacked edge to edge at the left, like book spines, where only the first letters of their titles show, clipped by the sliver. Clicking a sliver brings its card back. 48px under the band, the number of entries and a link to the full list sit at 17px on the left margin, so the stage does not end on an empty floor.
sections.mobile: No pin and no slivers. The cards stack at full width with 12px gaps, each in its tone, the title at 24px, the excerpt at 16px, the date and link at the foot. The heading sits above them at 10vw.

sections.name: Side facts, wide paragraph
sections.blueprint: Two rows share one vertical line at 34% of the viewport width. Row one: in a 160px column at the left margin, three label and value pairs stack with 20px between them, each a label in the soft ink with its value beneath in full ink, all at 13px (founded, based in, team size). From the 34% line a five-line paragraph at clamp(20px, 1.7vw, 26px), leading 1.35, runs to 90% of the width. Row two starts 120px lower and repeats the logic for the record of the practice: one plain word at 13px at the far left (awards, press, clients), then from the 34% line two list columns, each 260px wide with a 64px gutter, at 13px with 10px between lines: name at the left, year at the right in the soft ink. No heading; the paragraph opens the section. Each list comfortably holds 6–12 lines. No photographs are needed.
sections.mobile: Everything aligns to the left margin. The paragraph comes first at 19px. The three label and value pairs follow as a two-column grid at 14px. The two record lists stack with 40px between them, each opened by its plain word in full ink.

sections.name: A band per question
sections.blueprint: Each question owns a full-bleed band, and the bands alternate between two flat tones (ground and one step away, or two palette colours with their assigned inks) and butt together with no gap. Inside every band the same grid applies: the question in columns 1–5 at 28–32px bold, top-aligned with 56px of padding above; the answer in columns 7–12 at 18px with leading 1.5, the same padding, and 56px below. Bands are as tall as their content, so their heights differ, which gives the stack its rhythm. Four to seven bands. The heading is the first band: two to four words at about 7vw on the accent colour, flush left, taller than the rest at about 40svh with the words anchored to its bottom-left. All answers are visible; there are no toggles.
sections.mobile: Bands stay full-bleed and alternate. Inside each, the question at 22px then the answer at 17px, with 32px padding top and bottom and 20px at the sides. The heading band is 30svh tall with its words at 13vw at the bottom-left.

sections.name: Sentence, portrait, two links
sections.blueprint: One closing row of three elements hanging from the same top line, with open ground between them, on a 12-column grid. Columns 1–5: a sentence of 12–18 words at clamp(26px, 3vw, 44px), four lines, leading 1.1, saying what kind of enquiries are welcome; it is set as a paragraph and there is no separate heading. Columns 8–9: one small square portrait or photograph of the place, 150–170px, with square corners. Columns 10–12: a short question at 18px in medium weight, then 20px below it two underlined links stacked at 18px (the email address and one booking or social link), and beneath them a line at 14px in the soft ink with the city and the usual reply time. Columns 6–7 stay empty. The row has 160px of space above and 120px below. No form. On a dark ground the photograph is the only bright thing in the row.
sections.mobile: The sentence comes first at 7.4vw. Below it the portrait at 96px square sits at the left margin with the question and the two links to its right, top-aligned, in the remaining width. The city and reply-time line spans the full width beneath.

references.name: Applied Imagination
references.idea: An essay conceived on a flight is read as a descent: an altimeter ticks from 30,000 ft to zero while you scroll down through halftone clouds to mountains at ground level.
references.hero: A pale blue sky fading to warm cream fills the viewport, with white clouds shaded in halftone dots. A tiny serif logotype sits top-centre; no nav. The title, two centred lines of black wedge-serif at 8.9vw, occupies the middle half of the screen and about 73% of its width; a cloud layer passes in front of the second line's baseline so the feet of the letters dissolve into dots. A two-line centred deck at 24px sits beneath. A mono byline strip is centred on the bottom edge with a scroll cue bottom-right. On the left edge at mid-height, a short vertical rule carries a two-line mono altitude readout.
references.type: fsKim, a sturdy wedge-serif display face, regular weight at 128px with -0.01em tracking for the title and pull quotes; gtAmerica at 24px for the deck and about 16px for essay body; gtAmericaMono uppercase around 11px with wide tracking for byline, altitude and tape labels.
references.colour: #cbe4f2 #f1e3b5 #0a0a0a #ffc013 #8e2f8f #f04e23 — Sky blue melting into sand yellow is the constant ground and text is black. Saturated magenta, orange and yellow arrive only in collage objects, tape labels and the footer contact card.
references.imagery: Photo-collage cut-outs (parachutes carrying a treasure chest and a burning dumpster, a pair of legs, mountains) given a coarse halftone dot screen, layered in front of and behind the type against painted clouds.
references.layout: A narrow text column about 38% wide for essay passages, interrupted by full-width display pull quotes and collage objects floating at the edges. One continuous sky instead of sections, with a fixed left-edge altimeter. Nearly 23 screens, ending on a ground-level landscape.

sections.description: Sky background, no container. A three-line pull quote in black wedge-serif at about 7vw is centred and tightly leaded. Two cut-out parachutes hang over it: a magenta one from the top-left carrying a chest spilling coins, an orange one at lower right carrying a burning dumpster, each overlapping letterforms. Small mono labels on tilted strips of coloured tape are stuck to the objects. Words in the quote turn from grey to black as they are reached.

Running essay text in about 16px grotesk, black, in a single column roughly 38% of the viewport wide, positioned left of centre with large sky margins on both sides. Paragraphs are separated by a blank line; serif sub-statements at about 28px introduce passages. The next display quote is seen rising from below, its letters partly hidden behind cloud and blurred.

Ground level: halftone-screened mountains in green and brown rise from both sides, and the title returns at huge scale, cropped by the top edge and tucked behind the peaks. Centred below is a square-cornered two-panel card: a cream left panel with a short form of two fields and a small orange button, and a magenta right panel with a round portrait, name and a yellow subscribe button. Yellow tape-strip credits sit on the bottom edge.

steal: Tie a persistent numeric readout to scroll position (altitude falling to zero) so the reader's progress becomes part of the story.
Layer an illustration element in front of the bottom of a giant title so the letters sink into the scene instead of sitting on top.
Apply one coarse halftone dot screen to every photo cut-out so collage pieces from different sources read as one illustration set.

references.name: Artem Taradash
references.idea: A designer's CV compressed into one newspaper-like band at the top, after which oversized product renders and project artefacts speak at full scale.
references.hero: White page with 20px margins. Top-left are three small black rectangular tags with white text (name and two links). Below them a three-line statement at about 3vw in regular-weight grotesk fills the first third, left-aligned. To its right, starting at the very top edge, run two narrow columns of 12px text, then a third column listing clients one per line, and in the far top-right a circular portrait about 200px wide with a white hand-lettered word across the face. This text band ends by a quarter of the height. Below it a huge cut-out vehicle render bleeds off the bottom, with a project card at right.
references.type: One family, Diatype, in regular weight throughout. Three sizes: about 43px for statements and project titles, 12.4px for all running text, about 11px for tags. Tight leading, sentence case, no bold and no capitals; hierarchy comes from size alone.
references.colour: #ffffff #111111 #f7f9fb #1c4fd8 #f0a23a — Strictly black on white for the frame. All colour arrives with project material: an orange-to-blue gradient, a cobalt zigzag pattern, warm photography.
references.imagery: Product renders cut out on white and shown very large, interface screenshots with a small corner radius, a full-width studio photo with a circular logo overlaid, and textile-pattern fields running margin to margin. Scale varies sharply between projects.
references.layout: A loose six-column grid with 20px margins; small text blocks hang from column lines beside very large images. Each project is arranged differently, and there are no dividers or section backgrounds, only white space and jumps in scale. The tag nav stays fixed top-left.

sections.description: Each project pairs one oversized visual with a small caption cluster. In the first, a cut-out product render fills the left 60% and bleeds off the edge. The right third stacks a landscape screenshot with slightly rounded corners, then a row holding a tiny label and two-line title at about 3vw on the left and a five-line 12px description on the right.

A row of three: a round black watch-face mock-up about a quarter of the width, a wide rectangle filled with a horizontal blue, violet, orange, blue gradient with a tiny tick scale beneath it, and a narrow text column at far right with label, three-line title and two short paragraphs. Circle, rectangle and text share a top line.

A cobalt-and-white zigzag textile pattern runs margin to margin for more than a full viewport height with only a two-line caption beneath it at left. Before it, a black-backed mosaic of pattern samples and report-cover mock-ups sits beside two narrow text columns. The pattern is given a section to itself with no mock-up frame.

Closing row on white: a tiny label, then a four-line sentence at about 3vw in the left third; a small square portrait at the two-thirds mark; to its right a short question with two underlined links below. All three hang from the same top line with empty space between them.

steal: Put bio, client list and portrait in one compact multi-column band at the top so the first scroll is already work.
Use solid black rectangular tags with white text as the only navigation chrome.
Let one project artefact (a pattern, a gradient) run full width for a whole screen with a two-line caption instead of framing it in a mock-up.

references.name: Neutomni
references.idea: A small web studio sells its websites like packaged goods, printed in one red ink on white paper: the preloader is a cut-along-the-line coupon, the prices are tear-off tickets with barcodes, and the process is a square wheel that rounds off as the bumpy road from A to B smooths out.
references.hero: White page with 20px margins. A full-width red wordmark 1400x230 (97% of the width, 26% of the height) runs across the top; 10px under it a 13px row holds a one-line descriptor at the left, the nav from the centre line at x=720 and an italic email flush right. The 52px headline sits in the right half from x=720, two upright sans lines and a closing line in italic serif. A dark 576x360 video card of case-study screens is centred at the bottom and cropped by the fold, about 230px showing. Small local time and a pulsing open-for-work dot sit in the bottom corners. No button.
references.type: Three voices. A neutral grotesque at 400 (61% of characters) for headings and 16px body at 1.2 leading; an italic high-contrast serif (19%) that always takes the closing clause of a headline; a monospace (19%) for 13px uppercase labels, the process equation and price lines. Fixed steps of 118px (8.2vw), 80, 60, 52 and 32px, no clamp(), nothing bold, leading 1.0 for the sans and 0.9 for the italic. The house rules ban the italic accent clause and the monospace: one face per headline, labels in the text face.
references.colour: #cf1830 #ffffff #1a1a1a #6db1f0 #f8f4f4 — One ink: red for 63% of all text (5.5:1 on white) and for a few full grounds (preloader, process columns, footer, one price card) on a white page. A near-black band for the reel, and one sky blue saved for the pricing scene, where the site floods it in as a rising glow; the house version cuts to a flat sky field.
references.imagery: Staged mockup photographs of the studio's sites on real devices in real scenes (a monitor in a hedge, a tablet in robot arms, a phone on a desk) in soft daylight, square corners; a small founders photo; a 38s looping reel of case-study screens; white line drawing for the process. Only the price tickets get rounded corners and soft shadows.
references.layout: 20px margins, and the page is built on its centre line: the nav, the hero headline, the founders photo and the counter-statements all start at x=720 while the left half holds small metadata or the opposite statement. Sections butt against each other with no conventional padding; runways of about 3448px (process), 2288px (work) and 7080px (pricing) carry the pinned scenes, so 450 words fill about 24 screens.

sections.description: Split on the centre line: a 60px four-line statement from x=20 in the left half, and a small founders photograph 340x165 dropped at x=720 beside it.

Pinned for about 4 viewports on a 1400x900 stage: four red columns about 340px wide with 12px gaps rise from the bottom as a stepped bar chart until all reach about 720px. One white drawing runs across all four: a dashed guide at about 30% of the height, a wavy road below it that flattens column by column, and an outline shape that rolls along the guide and turns from square to circle. Each column ends in a 20px title and a three-line description in white.

A sticky split: a two-line 118px section title at the top left and a three-row project index at the bottom left (32px italic names, the active row in full red, the others faded), facing a staged device photograph that takes 60-65% of the width and the full height, bleeding off the right edge and wiping in with a clip-path for each project.

A sky-blue field rises from the bottom until it floods the screen; an 80px centred white headline blurs its upright lines while the closing line stays sharp, and three ticket cards fly up tilted in 3D perspective, two white receipts with a perforated edge and a barcode and one red card.

steal: Print with one ink: every word in a single saturated colour on a white ground, with a second hue kept for one late scene so it lands as an event, not a theme.

Tell a process with one drawing that crosses all the step blocks (a shape turning from square to circle while the road under it flattens) inside a pinned stage of 3-4 viewports, and keep the blocks as plain colour with a short title and three lines of copy.

Turn pricing into objects you could tear off and keep: ticket cards with a perforated edge and a drawn barcode, tilted 5-15 degrees in perspective. Under the house rules they carry no resting shadow and the price is set in the text face, not monospace.
references.media: Media covers about 35% of the first screen: the full-width wordmark across the top and a video card peeking from the fold, which grows into a sticky full-screen dark reel. Later pictures are a small photograph on the centre line, staged device photographs filling 60-65% of the width in a sticky split, and a canvas stage of rising red columns; one 38s looping video with no poster.
references.motion: A 3.5s red preloader in which scissors travel along a dotted cut line, the wordmark already in its final place. Under Lenis, lines blur and rise in at 'top 85%' over 0.52-0.64s power1.out with a 0.12s stagger, the process shape morphs over 1s power2.inOut, the work pin scrubs at 0.8 with 0.9s power2.inOut clip-path wipes and inactive rows at 0.28 opacity, and the pricing runway runs about 7000px with no reduced-motion rule.
